objective: Explain and preserve breadth-first traversal invariants.

coaching_cards.title: Protect the visited-set invariant
coaching_cards.misconception: A traversal can enqueue the same node through two parents unless it marks nodes when they enter the frontier.
coaching_cards.corrective_question: What prevents node D from entering the frontier twice when B and C both point to it?
coaching_cards.hint: Ask: when is a node recognized by the traversal, and can another parent add it before that moment?

mutation.symptom: D can enter the frontier twice through B and C.

scaffolds.observation: D is reachable from both B and C during the same traversal level.
scaffolds.question: What invariant should prevent a node from entering the frontier more than once?

scaffolds.observation: Trace the moment B adds D, then the moment C considers D before D leaves the frontier.
scaffolds.question: At each moment, what does the traversal know about D?

scaffolds.observation: Describe the frontier-entry precondition without writing code.
scaffolds.question: What must be true of every node immediately after it enters the frontier?

confirmation.observation: Your diagnosis identifies a delay between discovering D and recording that discovery.
confirmation.question: At which abstract lifecycle event must the traversal record a node to preserve the invariant?
